title: Security gating: SSO/RBAC/KMS acceptance criteria and evidence inventory
creator: Maya Chen
description: Purpose: Define a single operational playbook and evidence matrix for gating Private/VPC deployments on core security controls (SSO/SAML federation, RBAC enforcement, audit logging, and KMS/HSM key custody). This ticket scopes the PRD clarifications, acceptance criteria, and the exact artefacts required for stakeholder sign-off (Security PM, Compliance, Engineering, Customer Success). Background: multiple earlier PRDs assumed different evidence formats and retention windows; this work normalizes acceptance to reduce onboarding friction for enterprise customers and to make audits reproducible. Scope: - SSO/SAML: metadata exchange, SP/IdP validation, test accounts, automated SSO smoke tests, logout/relay state behavior. - RBAC: canonical role manifest, bootstrap admin workflow, delegated operator roles, session expiry policy, audit-able policy changes. - Audit logs: schema, retention (default 365 days with tiered retention for enterprise), tamper-evidence, ingest pipeline proof. - KMS/HSM: CMK creation workflow, rotation policy, backup/escape-hatch procedures, HSM attestation evidence for on-prem deployments. Out of scope: UI polish for console role editor (tracked separately under DES-12211).
acceptance_criteria: 1) SSO/SAML: - SAML metadata file uploaded or available via URL and validated in CI. - End-to-end SSO test (IdP -> SP -> SAML assertion -> token exchange) passes in staging and is documented in test-plan.md. - Example SAML assertion captured (redacted) and stored in evidence bundle. 2) RBAC: - Role manifest (YAML) published to repository and referenced by runtime. - All privileged actions require an approved role; no direct root token use permitted. - Policy change audit trail exists and is queryable via Console for at least 90 days. 3) Audit logs: - Event schema documented (timestamp, actor_id, src_ip, resource, action, outcome, correlation_id). - Logs pipeline demonstrates delivery to customer-owned S3/Cloud Storage or Redwood-managed encrypted bucket. - Tamper-evidence test (log hashing/chain) passes in demo and is documented. 4) KMS/HSM: - Customer CMK creation flow exercised and rotation tested in staging. - HSM attestation (for on-prem) with vendor-signed report attached to evidence. - Key usage logs are emitted and linked to audit events. 5) Evidence package: - For each of the above, there is at least one artifact: config file, test output, PR link, and a short narrative (<= 250 words) describing the verification steps. - All artifacts collected into the compliance EVIDENCE ZIP and uploaded to Confluence page linked below.
signoff_checklist: Stakeholders: Security PM (Maya Chen), Compliance Lead (E. Rivera), Lead SRE (A. Patel), Product Manager (this ticket), Customer Success representative. Steps: 1) Compile evidence bundle with the following files: - saml_metadata.xml (or URL) - saml_end_to_end_test_output.txt - role_manifest.yaml - rbac_policy_change_log_sample.json - audit_event_schema.md - sample_audit_events.log - kms_rotation_proof.txt - hsm_attestation.pdf - deployment_playbook.md 2) Internal review: Security PM validates artifacts -> mark 'security_approved' 3) Compliance review: confirm retention, data residency, and evidence format -> mark 'compliance_approved' 4) SRE validation: run smoke tests in canary -> attach run IDs and latencies -> mark 'sre_approved' 5) Customer Success: verify onboarding checklist applies to customers in pilot -> mark 'cs_approved' 6) Final sign-off: Exec sponsor (VP Product or VP Security) signs the signoff memo copied to legal. Notes on edge cases: - If HSM attestation missing for specific customer, require compensating controls documented and approved by Compliance. - For customers requiring >365d retention, capture expected additional contract terms in the evidence bundle.
decisions: - Use SAML 2.0 with metadata exchange as canonical onboarding method; OIDC will be a separate adapter tracked in PM-43112. - RBAC model: prefer role-based with hierarchical role inheritance rather than attribute-only policies to simplify audit statements. - Default audit retention is 365 days; enterprise SKUs can opt for custom retention via contract. - KMS: support both Redwood-managed KMS and customer-managed keys (CMKs); HSM-based keys required for air-gapped on-prem installs. Rationale recorded in decision-log.md.
tradeoffs: - Strict RBAC (least privilege) increases onboarding effort for customers with ad-hoc roles; mitigated with a templated role_manifest and quick-start scripts. - Long audit retention increases storage costs; mitigated by tiered cold storage and summarization indexes. - Requiring HSM attestation for on-prem slows onboarding under procurement-heavy customers; alternative: temporary escrowed key workflow with stricter monitoring.
